closed_review_findings.scenario: CallAPITyped discarded HTTP202/unresolved3xx status, allowing terminal-looking result data to reconcile a pending receipt.
closed_review_findings.resolution: Domain now retains raw ApiResp and requires final HTTP200 before status parsing/reconciliation; malformed or nonfinal proof stops immediately.

closed_review_findings.detected_in: uncommitted initial integration, reported directly to both owners before final commits
closed_review_findings.scenario: Existing default GET redirect policy could follow to another ticket/origin and return200, while reconciliation inferred the original configured origin.
closed_review_findings.resolution: Exact native status-request marker makes default redirect policy return the original3xx with no target request; ordinary unmarked/download redirects retain behavior. Domain rejects the original non200 response.

closed_review_findings.scenario: A status0+token result could remain an unknown import because its type/source/target/error contradicted the create, yet still trigger bot full_access grant on the returned token.
closed_review_findings.resolution: RunImport now requires pure exact-create-body completion proof and successful receipt persistence before a dependent bot grant; standalone recovery requires direct native status and supported noncontradictory target.

limitations: Approval covers the named Drive follow-up scopes at exact path hashes, not unrelated changes in pre-existing files or the entire release.

No live, model, broad unit or process reruns were performed by this reviewer. Unit/race/process artifacts lack embedded tested source revision/hash binding; owners associate them with final committed files, recorded without inferring immutable execution provenance. The separate detached-checkout source-lint log explicitly binds032b922.

Native optional source/destination echoes are validated when present; direct same-ticket authenticated HTTP200 job_status0 with requested type/token is the completion contract when echoes are omitted. No cross-invocation reconciliation is provided.

Post-rename directory fsync failure can leave an applied file visible while the invocation retains unknown with persistence_failed and exit22; no durable-success claim is made in that case. Windows directory-fsync limitation is inherited.
